'''Lenka Zdeborová''' (born 24 November 1980){{r|cv}} is a [[Czechs|Czech]] physicist and computer scientist who applies methods from [[statistical physics]] to [[machine learning]] and [[constraint satisfaction problem]]s. She is a professor of [[physics]] and [[computer science]] and [[Communications system|communication systems]] at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

== Life ==
Zdeborová was born in [[Plzeň]] and attended a local grammar school where she excelled in math and physics. After living in [[France]] with her family and working at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS), she and her partner moved to [[Switzerland]] in 2020. They are currently raising their two [[Child|children]] there.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nejezchlebová |first=Lenka Vrtišková |date=2022-11-30 |title=I'm not afraid of the machines taking over. I worry that we might fail to harness their capabilities in time |url=https://www.universitas.cz/en/people/9696-i-m-not-afraid-of-the-machines-taking-over-i-worry-that-we-might-fail-to-harness-their-capabilities-in-time |access-date=2024-05-08 |website=Universitas, magazín vysokých škol |language=en}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Zdeborová earned a master's degree in physics at [[Charles University]] in 2004, and 2008, completed an international dual doctorate ("en cotutelle") at both [[Charles University]] and [[University of Paris-Sud]]. Her [[doctoral advisor]]s were Václav Janiš at [[Charles University]], and [[Marc Mézard]] at Paris-Sud.{{r|cv}}

After postdoctoral research at the Center for Nonlinear Studies of [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], she became a researcher for the French [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|Centre National de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) in 2010, posted at the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]]'s [[Institut de physique théorique - IPhT Saclay]] in [[Paris-Saclay]]. She also earned a [[habilitation]] in 2015 at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)]].{{r|cv}} After receiving her [[habilitation]], she undertook a research fellowship in [[Los Alamos, New Mexico|Los Alamos]], [[New Mexico]]. Since 2020, she has been working at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) as an Associate Professor of physics, and of computer science and communication systems in the Schools of Basic Sciences and  of Computer and Communication Sciences (IC), and is the head of Laboratory of Statistical Physics of Computation.<ref name=":0"/><ref name=":1"/>

==Recognition==
Zdeborová won the [[CNRS Gold medal|CNRS Bronze medal]] in 2014.{{r|cv}} In 2016, the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale supérieure (Paris)]] gave her the Philippe Meyer Prize in theoretical physics for her work in Statistical Physics of Disordered Systems.{{r|pmp}} She is the 2018 winner of the [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize]] for young female scientists earned by standing out throughout her career.{{r|pijc}}. She was also received the [[Josiah Willard Gibbs Lectureship]] of the American Mathematics Society and gave her Gibbs lecture in 2021. In 2022, she was awarded the Alternative Fields Medal.{{r|afm}}
